reviews.reason: The reports show `owned` dereferencing a nil reminder, and the diagnosis identifies `Store.Get` returning `(nil, nil)` for deleted reminders as the source. Returning `ErrNotFound` in that branch fixes the contract violation at the store boundary, allowing the existing API error mapping to respond with 404.

The UTC-aligned truncation can select the previous local calendar day, causing `Weekly.Next` to return an occurrence before `after` and ultimately a negative digest day index. Starting the search at local midnight fixes the scheduling logic at its source rather than merely guarding the digest crash.

The nil-pointer panic stems from Store.Get returning the invalid (nil, nil) pair for tombstoned reminders, which is the shared upstream cause of both the GET and mark-done crashes in API.owned. Setting err = ErrNotFound in the deleted branch restores the invariant at the source instead of patching each handler, so both endpoints now correctly 404.

The diagnosis identifies nil preferences on imported users as the cause, and initializing `Prefs` in `ImportUsers` fixes the problem at the source. The sender lookup change does not address nil preferences, but it is supplementary and does not undermine the fix.

The nil-map lookup explains the panic, but the change only converts it into a send error: `ValidChannel` still accepts `sms` even though no sender is registered. Reject unsupported channels when preferences are set (or provide an SMS sender), while retaining the defensive check in `SendNow`.

The panic is caused by `MarshalJSON` dereferencing a nil zone even though `Weekly.Location()` defines nil as UTC. Serializing that case as UTC fixes the inconsistency at the type’s serialization boundary; rejecting unknown zones in the API could be a separate behavior change, but is not required to fix this crash.

The crash is a nil dereference caused by `Store.Get` returning `(nil, nil)` for deleted reminders, which violates its contract. The fix corrects that at the source by returning `ErrNotFound`, so every caller that checks `err` is protected, and the diagnosis reports a reproducer confirming the 500-to-404 change.

The panic is a downstream symptom: Weekly.Next could return an occurrence before its `after` argument because Truncate(24h) floors on a UTC-aligned boundary that lands on the previous local date in western zones, so the diagnosis correctly identifies the root cause. Rebuilding midnight from the local year/month/day in Weekly.Next fixes the source rather than patching BuildDigest's day-index guard.

The nil Zone is treated as UTC elsewhere (Zone.Location, Next) so it is a valid state; the panic is a genuine nil dereference at serialization, and serializing nil Zone as "UTC" fixes it consistently with the rest of the package rather than merely suppressing the crash.

The fix only guards the crash site in MarshalJSON, while the diagnosis itself shows the nil Zone is created by POST accepting an unknown tz name and silently treating it as UTC. The right fix is at that boundary: reject or normalize invalid zones when the reminder is created, and make the marshaller's nil handling consistent with that.

The divide-by-zero in Every.Next is correctly traced to parseEvery accepting a zero interval, and the fix validates at that input boundary plus guards Next against invalid directly-constructed values, which is the right place rather than only suppressing the panic.

The stack and request evidence point to `parseEvery` accepting a zero interval, which later causes division by zero in `Every.Next`. Rejecting nonpositive intervals at parse time prevents invalid schedules from being stored, fixing the cause rather than merely guarding the panic site.

The crash is traced to Weekly.Next returning a time before `after` because Truncate(24h) rounds to a UTC midnight, and the diff fixes that rule by building midnight from the local calendar date. The reasoning that BuildDigest should not need to handle negative indexes is sound, and a reproducer and unit regressions cover the case.

The panic came from passing user-controlled, unvalidated timezone data to `must.Get`; validating `req.TZ` when preferences are saved prevents new invalid values. Handling `LoadLocation` errors in `digest` also protects against previously stored or otherwise invalid values, fixing the issue at both the input boundary and the crash site.

The root-cause analysis is right and the parseEvery check is the correct place to fix it, but the added guard in Every.Next returns the zero time, which store.Due treats as already due. That is the re-send-on-every-tick hazard the diagnosis itself says must be avoided, so the defence-in-depth change reintroduces the problem it warns about.

The panic is `close of closed channel` from Dispatcher.Stop unconditionally closing the stop channel, and wrapping the close in sync.Once makes Stop idempotent at the actual fault site, correctly handling both repeated and concurrent calls. The unrelated users.go/weekly.go diffs are noise but don't affect the fix.

The panic was caused by digest loading an arbitrary user-supplied TZ via must.Get, and the fix correctly addresses both sides: rejecting unknown zones at the write path (updatePrefs) and defensively falling back to UTC for already-persisted invalid data, so legacy values no longer crash digest requests.

The panic stems directly from parseClock indexing parts[1] without validating the split count, and the added len(parts)!=2 guard fixes it exactly at that origin, returning a parse error rather than merely recovering elsewhere. The unrelated users.go/notify.go edits don't affect this diagnosis.

The two stacks are consistent with nil `Prefs` being dereferenced at different points in notification delivery. Defaulting missing preferences in `ImportUsers` fixes the missing user invariant at the source, rather than merely guarding the notification code.

The root cause (ImportUsers leaving Prefs nil, unlike AddUser) and the users.go nil-Prefs default fix are correct and in the right place. However, the notify.go changes are unexplained by the diagnosis: they remove the "sms" channel, which is a user-visible behavior change, and add a nil-sender guard for a different path that the reported nil-Prefs crash does not hit. That bundles out-of-scope changes into the fix.

The root cause and the SendNow nil-Sender guard plus removing "sms" from the channel list are sound. However, the diff also changes store/users.go to default nil Prefs on load, which the diagnosis never mentions and which its own evidence rules out as the cause (usr_bo.Prefs was non-nil), so this unexplained behavior change should be removed or justified separately.

The diagnosis connects the negative day offset to `Weekly.Next` truncating a local time on the UTC-based 24-hour boundary, which can select the prior local calendar date. Building candidates from `local.Date()` fixes the date calculation at its source rather than guarding the digest index.

The root cause is correctly identified as must.Get being applied to user-supplied preference data, which the codebase otherwise handles by falling back to UTC via schedule.LookupZone. The fix replaces that misuse at the correct layer and matches the existing convention, with a reproducer that fails before and passes after. Validating zones on PUT /v1/me/prefs would be a worthwhile follow-up but does not change this fix.

BuildDigest is the function that computes the day index, so an occurrence before `from` legitimately yields a negative offset that must be filtered alongside offsets beyond `days`; the symmetric guard (i < 0 || i >= days) fixes the root cause at the indexing site rather than merely masking the crash.

The panic at notify.go:135 stems from SendNow indexing senders with a channel that ValidChannel advertised but NewDispatcher never registered (sms), and the fix corrects this at the source by removing sms from ValidChannel while also guarding against the nil-sender and nil-prefs dereferences at the crash site. The added store default for missing Prefs further removes a related nil-dereference path, so the change addresses the root cause rather than only masking the crash.

The crashes occur because `Store.Get` returns `(nil, nil)` for deleted reminders, which lets `owned` dereference a nil reminder. Returning `ErrNotFound` at the store boundary matches its documented behavior and lets callers handle the missing reminder without a panic.

Both crashes trace to `API.owned` dereferencing a nil reminder returned by `Store.Get`, which violated its error-based contract by returning (nil, nil) for tombstoned reminders; fixing the store to return ErrNotFound corrects the shared root cause for both GET and mark-done paths rather than only guarding the crash site. The change is at the right place and restores consistent 404 behavior.

store.Get returning (nil, nil) for tombstoned reminders violates the contract its callers rely on, and that is what both stack traces dereference at owned's rem.UserID check. The fix returns ErrNotFound at the source, matching the unknown-ID path, so all call sites are covered without guarding the crash site.

The crash is caused by `parseEvery` accepting a zero interval that `Every.Next` later uses as a divisor. Rejecting non-positive intervals at parsing prevents invalid schedules from being stored, fixing the cause rather than merely guarding the division.

The diagnosis identifies a plausible upstream cause, and validating the zone during creation is appropriate. However, this only prevents future invalid reminders; existing nil-zone records can still make GET /v1/reminders panic, so the reported crash is not fully fixed.

The crash is caused by a zero Interval reaching Every.Next, and parseEvery is the validation boundary where the invalid duration enters the system, so rejecting non-positive intervals there fixes the root cause rather than merely guarding the crash site in Next. The reproducer and test suite confirm it works.

The diagnosis traces the panic back to Weekly.Next, where Truncate(24h) rounds to a UTC midnight, so the search starts on the wrong local day and can return a firing before `after`. The fix builds local midnight in the rule's zone, which addresses the producer that breaks the Upcoming contract rather than adding a guard in BuildDigest.

The crash comes from Every.Next dividing by a zero Interval that parseEvery accepted from the user's "every 0s" input. Rejecting non-positive intervals at parse time fixes the bad input at its validation point, and the reproducer covers it. The only gap is that Every values built outside parseEvery would still reach Next unchecked.

The diagnosis correctly traces the panic to an unvalidated stored timezone reaching `must.Get(time.LoadLocation(...))` in the digest handler. Validating preferences before storage fixes the root cause, and handling load errors in the digest also protects against previously stored invalid values.

The diagnosis itself traces the nil zone to the create path, where an unresolvable timezone is accepted and persisted by parseWeekly. The change only guards the MarshalJSON crash site, so invalid rules still get stored and the bad input is silently treated as UTC instead of being rejected at creation. The fix should validate the timezone in createReminder or parseWeekly, not just make the read path tolerate nil.

The store/users.go fix correctly addresses the nil Prefs root cause in ImportUsers, but the diff also removes "sms" from channels and adds a sender-lookup guard in SendNow. Neither is covered by the diagnosis, and the guard does not prevent the nil Prefs dereference, since u.Prefs.Channel is still read before it. Those changes should be split out or justified.

The notify.go changes correctly remove the undeliverable "sms" channel and guard SendNow, but the store/users.go hunk defaulting nil Prefs is not explained by the diagnosis or any crash report. That unrelated behavior change should be split out or justified before filing.

The crash is a repeat/concurrent call to Dispatcher.Stop closing an already-closed channel, and guarding the close with sync.Once fixes it at the true source (Stop itself) rather than at the admin handler that happened to trigger it. The unrelated schedule/weekly.go edits don't undermine the correctness of this fix.

The panic is a nil dereference of w.Zone.Name in Weekly.MarshalJSON, and since nil Zone is a supported state (Zone.Location already treats nil as UTC), handling nil in MarshalJSON is the correct place to fix serialization consistently. The regression test confirms the panic and the fix aligns marshaling with the rest of the code's nil-zone semantics.

The panic is a genuine out-of-range index in parseClock when the clock string lacks a colon-separated minute ("20" splits to length 1), and adding a length check at that parse boundary returns a proper error that propagates up, fixing the root cause at the right place rather than merely guarding the caller. The extra unrelated changes (stopOnce, nil Zone handling) are harmless.

The crash stems from accepting and persisting an unrecognized IANA zone (Europe/Lisboa) via updatePrefs, then treating that user-controlled data as an invariant with must.Get in the digest handler. The fix correctly validates at the write path (rejecting with 400) and also hardens the digest read path against legacy data, addressing the root cause rather than just the crash site.

The diagnosis identifies must.Get wrapping time.LoadLocation on stored user data as the defect, and digest is the only direct LoadLocation caller, with other paths already using the nil-tolerant schedule.LookupZone convention. The fix matches that convention and is verified by a reproducer that fails before and passes after. Validating the zone on PUT /v1/me/prefs would be a useful complement, but it is not required for this fix.
